### The Higher Group of Five 3. 127

19. Then <term>Raga</term> <gloss>Lust</gloss>, the daughter of <term>Mara</term> <gloss>the Tempter</gloss>, spoke this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

Having cut through craving, the flood that sweeps away the crowd,
surely many beings will cross over.
Truly, this homeless one <note>original: "anoko"</note> will cut them off
and lead this great multitude to the far shore, away from the King of Death.

20. Great heroes, the <term>Tathagatas</term> <gloss>Thus-Gone Ones</gloss>, lead by means of the <term>Saddhamma</term> <gloss>True Teaching</gloss>. When beings are being led by the <term>Dhamma</term> <gloss>Truth</gloss>, what envy can there be for those who have direct knowledge?

21. Then <term>Tanha</term> <gloss>Craving</gloss>, <term>Arati</term> <gloss>Discontent</gloss>, and <term>Raga</term> <gloss>Lust</gloss>, the daughters of Mara, went to where Mara the Evil One was.

22. Mara the Evil One saw <term>Tanha</term>, <term>Arati</term>, and <term>Raga</term> coming from a distance. Having seen them, he addressed them in verses:

Fools! You tried to crush a mountain with lotus stalks.
You dig into a mountain with your fingernails.
You chew iron with your teeth.
Having struck a rock with your heads, you seek a bottom in the abyss.
Having struck against a stump with your chests,
you turn away from <term>Gotama</term> <gloss>the Buddha</gloss> in frustration.

23. In their radiant splendor they came: <term>Tanha</term>, <term>Arati</term>, and <term>Raga</term>. The Teacher swept them away right there, like the wind blows away a tuft of fallen cotton.

->The Third Group<-

->The Summary of Titles<-

The Many Monks, Samiddhi, Godhika, The Seven Years, and The Daughters. This concludes the five-part section on Mara as taught by the Buddha. The Connected Discourses on Mara are complete.

<summary>This page concludes the Mara-samyutta, detailing the failure of Mara's daughters to tempt the Buddha and Mara's subsequent mockery of their efforts. It ends with a formal summary of the chapters included in this section of the Pali Canon.</summary>
